def-full-observed-and-missing-data:
## Definition

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ be a probability space and let
$W=(W_1,\ldots,W_k)$, for a finite $k\ge1$, be a random element of the product
measurable space $\mathcal W=\prod_{j=1}^k\mathcal W_j$
([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]],
[[def-measurable-space]]). The law of $W$ is the pushforward probability
measure defined in [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]]. Let
$\mathcal R$ be a nonempty finite set of observation patterns with its
discrete sigma-algebra, and let $R:\Omega\to\mathcal R$ be a random element.

For each $r\in\mathcal R$, specify the recorded coordinate set
$I_r\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}$ and its complement
$J_r=\{1,\ldots,k\}\setminus I_r$. The **observed projection**
$W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$ is the coordinate projection into
$\mathcal W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r):=\prod_{j\in I_r}\mathcal W_j$, and the
**missing projection** $W_{\mathrm{mis}}(r)$ is the projection into
$\mathcal W_{\mathrm{mis}}(r):=\prod_{j\in J_r}\mathcal W_j$. An empty
coordinate tuple takes values in a one-point measurable space. The **observed
record** is $O=(R,W_{\mathrm{obs}}(R))$ in the disjoint union
$\bigsqcup_{r\in\mathcal R}(\{r\}\times\mathcal W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r))$,
where a set in the disjoint-union sigma-algebra is measurable exactly when
each pattern section is measurable. The pattern records which coordinates are
available; it does not replace an unrecorded full-data value by zero.
def-mcar-mar-and-mnar:
## Definition

Fix the full-data/observed-data partition of
[[def-full-observed-and-missing-data]]. A **response mechanism** is a
specified conditional law $g(r\mid w)$ of the pattern $R$ given full data
$W=w$, represented by a probability kernel from the full-data space to the
finite pattern space
([[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]],
[[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]). In a parameterized model, write
the response kernel as $g_\psi$; it must be a probability distribution over
patterns for each full-data value.

Relative to a specified full-data law, the mechanism is **missing completely
at random (MCAR)** when, for every pattern $r$, $g(r\mid w)$ is constant in
$w$ almost surely. It is **missing at random (MAR)** when, for every pattern
$r$, there is a measurable function $h_r$ on that pattern's observed-data
space such that
$$g(r\mid w)=h_r(W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r))\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
For a family of full-data laws, the condition is required under each law with
the same response mechanism and observed-coordinate function. It is
**missing not at random (MNAR)** when MAR fails for at least one pattern, for
the declared full-data and observed-data partition. MCAR is a special case of
MAR, since a constant is a function of the observed coordinates.

These conditions concern a supplied version of the conditional law; values
off the full-data model's support do not affect the classification. This
definition does not assert that a response mechanism is empirically true or
that every joint law comes with a selected conditional kernel.
lem-observed-data-likelihood-under-respo:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $W=(W_1,\ldots,W_k)$ have a dominated full-data model with
finite pattern set $\mathcal R$ and a common sigma-finite product reference
measure $\nu=\bigotimes_{j=1}^k\nu_j$, where each $\nu_j$ is sigma-finite, and
selected finite-valued densities $p_\theta$ as in
[[def-dominated-statistical-experiment]] and [[def-likelihood-density]].
For each pattern $r$, put
$\nu_r^{\mathrm{obs}}=\bigotimes_{j\in I_r}\nu_j$ and
$\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}=\bigotimes_{j\in J_r}\nu_j$. Under the coordinate
reordering $w=(x,z)=(W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r),W_{\mathrm{mis}}(r))$, the reference
measure is $\nu_r^{\mathrm{obs}}\times\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}$. Empty coordinate
blocks are one-point spaces with unit mass. Let $g_\psi(r\mid w)$ be a supplied
response probability kernel as in
[[def-mcar-mar-and-mnar]], and form the joint model
$$P_{\theta,\psi}(dw,\{r\})=p_\theta(w)g_\psi(r\mid w)\,\nu(dw).$$
For a measurable set $A$ in the observed disjoint union, define
$\lambda_O(A)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\nu_r^{\mathrm{obs}}(\{x:(r,x)\in A\})$.
For each pattern $r$, the full-data marginal law of $W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$ has
density $\bar q_{\theta,r}(x)=\int p_\theta(x,z)\,\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}(dz)$.
The observed record $O=(R,W_{\mathrm{obs}}(R))$ is dominated by $\lambda_O$,
and its density at $(r,x)$ is
$$\ell_{\theta,\psi}(r,x)=\int p_\theta(x,z)g_\psi(r\mid x,z)\,\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}(dz).$$
thm-binary-outcome-mnar-nonidentificatio:
## Statement

Let $Y,R\in\{0,1\}$, with $R=1$ meaning that $Y$ is observed, and encode the
observed record as $O=(R,RY)$. Put
$$a=P(R=1),\qquad b=P(R=1,Y=1),\qquad 0\le b\le a\le1.$$
Let $\Theta_{a,b}$ be the set of all joint laws $P$ of $(Y,R)$ with these
values of $a$ and $b$, and let the statistical model map $P\in\Theta_{a,b}$
to the law of $O$. The full-data mean $m(P)=P(Y=1)$ is an estimand on this
model. Its set of values over $\Theta_{a,b}$ is exactly
$$[b,b+1-a].$$
Consequently, without a MAR restriction, the mean is not identifiable when
$a<1$; it is identified as $b$ when $a=1$. If MAR also holds, then for $a>0$
the mean is $b/a$, while for $a=0$ it remains unidentified.
thm-mar-ignorable-likelihood-factorizati:
## Statement

Assume AC and the hypotheses of
[[lem-observed-data-likelihood-under-response-model]]. Suppose the full-data
parameter and response-mechanism parameter range independently over the
Cartesian product $\Theta\times\Psi$, so the full-data density is $p_\theta$
and the response kernel is $g_\psi$. If MAR holds, write
$g_\psi(r\mid x,z)=h_{\psi,r}(x)$ for the pattern $r$ and observed value $x$.
For each $r$, put
$\bar q_{\theta,r}(x)=\int p_\theta(x,z)\,\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}(dz)$; this is
a density of the full-data marginal law of $W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$. Under AC,
choose a finite-valued density representative $q_{\theta,r}$ of that
marginal density class. Then
$$\ell_{\theta,\psi}(r,x)=h_{\psi,r}(x)q_{\theta,r}(x)$$
is a selected observed-record likelihood version.
For a fixed response parameter with $h_{\psi,r}(x)>0$, the factor
$h_{\psi,r}(x)$ cancels from likelihood ratios in $\theta$. Profiling over
the same set $\Psi$ for each $\theta$ also multiplies the $\theta$ likelihood
by a factor independent of $\theta$. This licenses omission of the response
factor for likelihood inference about $\theta$ on its support. It does not
license omission when the target depends on $\psi$, or when the allowed
parameter pairs are not a Cartesian product.
